{{short description|American basketball player (born 2001)}} {{Use American English|date=July 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=December 2025}} {{Infobox basketball biography | name = Spencer Jones | image = | caption = | position = [[Power forward]] / [[small forward]] | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 7 | weight_lb = 225 | league = [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] | team = Denver Nuggets | number = 21 | birth_date = {{birth date and age|2001|6|14}} | birth_place = [[Shawnee Mission, Kansas]], U.S. | high_school = [[Bishop Miege High School|Bishop Miege]]
([[Roeland Park, Kansas]]) | college = [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]] (2019–2024) | draft_year = 2024 | career_start = 2024 | career_end = | years1 = {{nbay|2024|start}}–present | team1 = [[Denver Nuggets]] | years2 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024]]–[[2025–26 NBA G League season|2026]] | team2 = →[[Grand Rapids Gold]] | highlights = * Second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] (2023) }} '''Spencer Keith Jones''' (born June 14, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Denver Nuggets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).{{Cite web |last=Durando |first=Bennett |date=October 11, 2025 |title=Spencer Jones, Nuggets player, launches nonprofit to support school education |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2025/10/11/spencer-jones-nuggets-player-nonprofit-school/ |access-date=October 16, 2025 |website=The Denver Post}} He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford Cardinal]].{{cite web|title=Spencer Jones Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and More|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/j/jonessp01.html|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=September 18, 2024}} ==High school career== Jones attended [[Bishop Miege High School|Bishop Miege]] in [[Roeland Park, Kansas]], emerging as a key contributor for one of the state's most successful high school basketball programs during his tenure. In March 2018, Bishop Miege won the Kansas Class 4A Division I state championship, defeating McPherson 57–54 in the title game at Koch Arena in Wichita. Jones led all scorers with 23 points, while teammate [[Jeremiah Robinson-Earl]] added 18 points and 11 rebounds, helping fuel Bishop Miege's comeback victory.{{cite news|last=McDowell|first=Sam|title=These five KC high schools won state basketball titles. Here’s how they did it|url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/high-school/article206094779.html|work=The Kansas City Star|date=March 21, 2018|access-date=December 21, 2025}} As a senior, Jones led Bishop Miege in scoring (18.8 points per game), rebounds (8.0), steals (3.0) and blocks (2.5), and was regarded as a top national recruit in the class of 2019.{{cite news |last=Davidson |first=Bob |date=March 11, 2018 |title=Miege boys rally past McPherson |url=https://eu.salina.com/story/sports/high-school/2018/03/11/miege-boys-rally-past-mcpherson/13019836007/ |access-date=December 23, 2025 |work=Salina Journal}} ==College career== Jones played [[college basketball]] for the [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford Cardinal]], where he appeared in 146 games in five seasons and averaged 11.0 points, 4.1 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 1.1 steals all while shooting 43.9% from the field and 39.7% from the three-point line in 28.3 minutes per game.{{cite web|title=Spencer Jones – MEN'S BASKETBALL|url=https://gostanford.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/season/2023-24/player/spencer-jones|website=GoStanford.com|access-date=July 30, 2024}}{{cite web|title=NUGGETS SIGN SPENCER JONES TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-spencer-jones-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 30, 2024|access-date=July 30, 2024}} In 2023, he made the [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] second team{{cite web|first=Kevin|last=Borba|title=Spencer Jones earns All-Pac-12 second team honors|url=https://www.si.com/college/stanford/basketball/spencer-jones-earns-all-pac-12-second-team-honors|website=SI.com|date=March 7, 2023|access-date=July 30, 2024}} and ended up his college career as the school's all-time leader in games played with 146 and three-pointers with 315. Across his five seasons at Stanford, Jones developed a reputation as a durable, low-usage wing with strong perimeter shooting, defensive versatility and leadership experience, traits that would later shape his transition to the professional level.{{cite news|last=Kroner|first=Steve|title=Spencer Jones returning to Stanford for 5th season: ‘Unfinished business’|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/college/article/spencer-jones-returning-stanford-basketball-5th-17889753.php|work=San Francisco Chronicle|date=April 12, 2023|access-date=December 21, 2025}} Jones [[Graduation|graduated]] from Stanford in 2024 with an [[undergraduate degree]] in [[Management Science]] and [[Engineering]].{{Cite web |last=Deeks |first=Mark |date=October 1, 2025 |title=Nuggets Forward’s Bizarre Approach To LinkedIn |url=https://heavy.com/sports/nba/denver-nuggets/nuggets-forwards-bizarre-social-media-strategy-linkedin/ |access-date=October 16, 2025 |website=Heavy Sports}} ==Professional career== ===Denver Nuggets (2024–present)=== ====Early career==== After going undrafted in the [[2024 NBA draft]], Jones joined the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] for the [[2024 NBA Summer League]]{{cite web|title=TRAIL BLAZERS ANNOUNCE NBA 2K25 SUMMER LEAGUE 2024 ROSTER|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-announce-nba-2k25-summer-league-2024-roster|website=[[NBA.com|NBA]]|date=July 5, 2024|access-date=July 30, 2024}} and on July 30, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Denver Nuggets]]. His production with Grand Rapids contrasted with a more limited NBA role, where he was primarily used in situational lineups rather than as a regular rotation player.{{cite news|last=Durando|first=Bennett|title=How 2-way player Spencer Jones has emerged as defensive specialist option for Nuggets|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2025/11/11/spencer-jones-nuggets-defense-two-way-player/|work=The Denver Post|date=November 11, 2025|access-date=December 21, 2025}} ==== Breakthrough and increase in minutes (2025–26)==== Jones returned to the [[Denver Nuggets]] for the 2025–26 season on a two-way contract, continuing to split time between Denver and its [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Grand Rapids Gold]]. He entered the season primarily outside the regular rotation, with his role largely defined by situational defensive assignments and limited minutes.{{cite news |last=Durando |first=Bennett |date=November 11, 2025 |title=How 2-way player Spencer Jones has emerged as defensive specialist option for Nuggets |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2025/11/11/spencer-jones-nuggets-defense-two-way-player/ |access-date=December 23, 2025 |work=The Denver Post}} During an injury stretch in December 2025, Jones was used as a starter alongside [[Nikola Jokić]] and [[Peyton Watson]] as the Nuggets adjusted their lineup in the absence of [[Aaron Gordon]] and [[Christian Braun]]. Despite the lineup's temporary nature, Denver maintained one of the league's most efficient offenses during that span, with Jones contributing through screening, floor spacing and off-ball movement rather than high-usage scoring.{{cite news |last=Durando |first=Bennett |date=December 14, 2025 |title=How Nuggets are navigating injuries to keep cooking on offense with Peyton Watson, Spencer Jones starting |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2025/12/14/nuggets-starting-lineup-offense-nikola-jokic-spencer-jones-two-way/ |access-date=December 23, 2025 |work=The Denver Post}} On December 1, 2025, Jones put another career high in points against the [[Dallas Mavericks]], where he scored 28 points in 39 minutes, he also had five rebounds to pair with his points.{{Cite web |date=December 2, 2025 |title=Anthony Davis scores season-high 32 points as Dallas Mavericks beat Denver Nuggets 131-121 |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/texas/news/dallas-mavericks-beat-denver-nuggets-131-121-dec-1/?ftag=CNM-00-10aag7e |access-date=December 3, 2025 |publisher=[[CBS News]]}} [[Sports Illustrated]] cited Jones's efficiency and impact while starting games during Denver's injury-related rotation adjustments.{{cite news |last=Struck |first=Logan |date=December 22, 2025 |title=Nuggets Forward Earns Nod on ESPN's NBA All-Value Team |url=https://www.si.com/nba/nuggets/onsi/news/denver-nuggets-forward-earns-nod-espn-nba-all-value-team |access-date=December 23, 2025 |work=Sports Illustrated}} On February 5, 2026, following the trade of [[Hunter Tyson]] to the [[Brooklyn Nets]], the Nuggets were slightly below the [[luxury tax]], which allowed the team to convert Jones' [[two-way contract]] to a standard NBA contract on February 19.{{Cite web|title=Nuggets’ Spencer Jones gets standard contract|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/nuggets-spencer-jones-gets-standard-contract/|access-date=2026-02-06|website=[[CBS Sports]]|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|title=Nuggets trade Hunter Tyson, open roster spot to sign Spencer Jones|url=https://denversports.com/nba/denver-nuggets/trade-tyson-sign-jones/2128550|access-date=2026-02-06|website=DenverSports.com|language=en-US}} Jones averaged a career-high 5.5 points and 3.3 rebounds during the 2025–26 season, playing in 64 games and starting 37. During the [[2026 NBA playoffs]], he shot 69.2% on [[Three-point field goal|three-pointers]], the best in the NBA. Following his breakout season, Jones entered [[Restricted free agent (NBA)|restricted free agency]], where the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] signed him to a two-year, $12 million [[offer sheet#NBA|offer sheet]] on July 25.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49447641/spencer-jones-agrees-thunder-offer-nuggets-get-option-match|last=Charania|first=Shams|author-link=Shams Charania|title=Spencer Jones agrees to Thunder offer; Nuggets get option to match|date=July 25, 2026|website=ESPN|access-date=July 27, 2026}} The next day, the Nuggets matched the offer sheet, returning Jones to the team but sending them into the [[NBA salary cap#Second apron|second apron]].{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49459602/sources-nuggets-matching-okc-offer-sheet-spencer-jones|last=Charania|first=Shams|author-link=Shams Charania|title=Nuggets match Thunder's offer
